findings.claim: As White the player scores above the Elo expectation computed from pre-game ratings.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, all white games
findings.caveat: Expected score is the Elo formula on chess.com (Glicko) ratings with the opponent's pre-game rating reconstructed as post-game rating plus the player's rating change; the over-performance baseline over all games is positive (Q1), so compare families with the colour's overall value, not with zero.

findings.claim: As Black the player scores about at the Elo expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, all black games
findings.caveat: Elo expectation on Glicko ratings is approximate; 4 game(s) without usable ratings are left out of expected-score columns.

findings.section: What this means for the player
findings.claim: The player opens 1.e4 in the large majority of white games.
findings.metric: share of white games starting 1.e4

findings.claim: In 1.e4 games as White the player scores above the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, white games starting 1.e4
findings.caveat: 211 of these games are from the last 12 months; the 1.d4 alternative (346 games, 1 in the last 12 months) scores 0.045 [-0.002, 0.101] and is history.

findings.claim: In 1.e4 games as White the player and the opponents give away the same expected points in the opening phase.
findings.metric: sum of ep_loss over the opening-phase moves per game, player vs opponents in the same games; difference printed as opponents minus player (positive = opponents gave away more)
findings.caveat: The opening phase is the material heuristic (roughly the first 10-12 moves), well beyond book; ep_loss is relative to Stockfish 17.1 at 1M nodes.

findings.claim: In 1.e4 e5 games as Black the player scores at the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games starting 1.e4 e5
findings.caveat: Opening ep lost is the same for both sides in these games (opponents minus player -0.002 [-0.010, 0.005]).

findings.claim: In 1.d4 d5 games as Black the player scores at the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games starting 1.d4 d5
findings.caveat: Book gain is slightly negative in these games (-0.005 [-0.009, -0.001] ep), i.e. the known part of the line leaves the player marginally worse off than the ratings predict.

findings.claim: The Sicilian (1.e4 c5) as Black, played only in 2022, scored well below the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games starting 1.e4 c5
findings.caveat: player is the raw score (expected 0.44); difference is score minus expected. 0 games in the last 12 months (years 22): history, not a target. The player also gave away more than the opponents in the opening phase (opponents minus player -0.032 [-0.065, -0.001]).

findings.claim: The Italian Game, the player's most frequent white family, scores about at the colour's overall over-performance.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, white games in the Italian Game family
findings.caveat: Family is the text before the colon of the Lichess opening name; at this level names describe the first 2-4 moves.

findings.claim: The 'Zukertort Opening' as White (mostly the Tennison Gambit by transposition) scores clearly above the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, white games in the Zukertort Opening family
findings.caveat: Names are assigned by position, so this label mostly began e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4; 84 of 85 games are bullet, 6 in the last 12 months. Book gain is negative (-0.017 [-0.031, -0.003]): the engine dislikes the gambit, the results do not.

findings.claim: The Queen's Gambit Declined as White scored clearly above the rating expectation, but has not been played in the last 12 months.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, white games in the Queen's Gambit Declined family
findings.caveat: 0 games in the last 12 months (years 22-24); 55 of 73 are blitz. Many families are compared, so expect a few CIs to exclude zero by chance.

findings.claim: The Queen's Gambit Declined as Black scores clearly above the rating expectation and is still in use.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games in the Queen's Gambit Declined family
findings.caveat: 13 games in the last 12 months. Book gain is slightly negative (-0.008 [-0.013, -0.004]); the surplus comes from the opponents' opening-phase errors, see the matching comparison.

findings.claim: In the Queen's Gambit Declined as Black the opponents give away more expected points in the opening phase than the player.
findings.metric: sum of ep_loss over the opening-phase moves per game, player vs opponents in the same games; difference printed as opponents minus player (positive = opponents gave away more)
findings.caveat: In blitz alone the difference is 0.090 [0.047, 0.132] (45 games); in bullet 0.016 [-0.004, 0.036] (95 games).

findings.claim: The Bishop's Opening as Black scores clearly above the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games in the Bishop's Opening family
findings.caveat: 13 games in the last 12 months; as Black the family is the opponent's choice. In bullet alone 0.110 [0.018, 0.197] (96 games).

findings.claim: The Scandinavian Defense as Black scored above the rating expectation in a small, historic sample.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games in the Scandinavian Defense family
findings.caveat: 0 games in the last 12 months (years 22-23); CI barely excludes zero and many comparisons are made.

findings.claim: The Three Knights Opening as Black has the largest over-performance of any family, in a small historic sample.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games in the Three Knights Opening family
findings.caveat: 0 games in the last 12 months; as Black the family is the opponent's choice.

findings.claim: The Sicilian Defense as Black scored clearly below the rating expectation and was abandoned after 2022.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games in the Sicilian Defense family
findings.caveat: 0 games in the last 12 months (years 22): history, not a target.

findings.claim: Against the Zukertort Opening (1.Nf3) as Black the player scores clearly below the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, black games in the Zukertort Opening family
findings.caveat: 6 games in the last 12 months, so still relevant; in bullet alone -0.299 [-0.410, -0.167] (26 games). Opening-phase ep lost is not measurably different from the opponents' (-0.024 [-0.062, 0.012]), so the deficit arises later.

findings.claim: In bullet, the Italian Game as Black scores below the rating expectation.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, bullet black games in the Italian Game family
findings.caveat: Pooled over time classes the family is -0.033 [-0.084, 0.016] (373 games); in bullet the player also gives away more in the opening phase (opponents minus player -0.022 [-0.043, -0.003]).

findings.claim: In bullet games against the Scandinavian Defense the player gives away more expected points in the opening phase than the opponents.

findings.caveat: The family still scores at expectation in bullet (-0.008 [-0.069, 0.052]); the recurring move 2. f3 (31 times, all in 2022) explains part of the opening-phase loss.

findings.section: 3. Does staying in book longer help?
findings.claim: In bullet, games that stayed 9 or more plies in named theory score no better relative to expectation than games that left after 1-2 plies.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, bullet games with book_ply 9+ (1-2 plies: 0.020 [-0.015, 0.059], 618 games)
findings.caveat: Book depth is a joint property of both players and correlates with the opening family and the opponents' knowledge; not something the player can choose unilaterally. Book gain in the 9+ bin is -0.009 [-0.016, -0.002] ep.

findings.section: 3. Does staying in book longer help?
findings.claim: In blitz, games that stayed 9 or more plies in named theory score no better relative to expectation than games that left after 1-2 plies.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, blitz games with book_ply 9+ (1-2 plies: 0.052 [0.000, 0.114], 285 games)
findings.caveat: Book depth is a joint property of both players. In the blitz 9+ bin the opponents give away more in the opening phase (opponents minus player 0.030 [0.005, 0.055]).

findings.section: 3. Does staying in book longer help?
findings.claim: In rapid, games that stayed 9 or more plies in named theory score no better relative to expectation than games that left after 1-2 plies.
findings.metric: mean per game of score minus Elo expected score, rapid games with book_ply 9+ (1-2 plies: 0.014 [-0.090, 0.123], 85 games)
findings.caveat: Small bins; CIs are wide.

findings.section: 3. Does staying in book longer help?
findings.claim: Games typically leave the named opening lines after four plies.
findings.metric: median book_ply (depth of the deepest named line reached), all games with moves
findings.caveat: 75th percentile 6 plies; Lichess names at this level describe the first 2-4 moves.

findings.claim: In bullet the player is the side that leaves the named lines first in about two thirds of games.
findings.metric: share of games in which the player played the first move after the last book move
findings.caveat: A game leaves the list when either side plays something unnamed; opponents are rating-matched, so the share describes the player's repertoire relative to the field at that level.

findings.claim: In blitz the player is the side that leaves the named lines first in about two thirds of games.
findings.metric: share of games in which the player played the first move after the last book move

findings.claim: In rapid the player is the side that leaves the named lines first in about two thirds of games.
findings.metric: share of games in which the player played the first move after the last book move

findings.claim: In bullet the player's book-leaving move costs slightly less than the opponents' book-leaving moves, so the player leaves named lines by choice rather than by blundering.
findings.metric: ep_loss of the first move after the last book move, player's deviations vs opponents' deviations (disjoint sets of games); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: The two sets of games are disjoint, so the difference is an independent (not paired) bootstrap. In cp_loss: 39 [36, 42] vs 57 [53, 62].

findings.claim: In blitz the player's book-leaving move costs about the same as the opponents' book-leaving moves.
findings.metric: ep_loss of the first move after the last book move, player's deviations vs opponents' deviations (disjoint sets of games); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Independent bootstrap over disjoint game sets. In cp_loss: 46 [42, 50] vs 56 [51, 62].

findings.claim: In rapid the player's book-leaving move costs no more than the opponents' book-leaving moves.
findings.metric: ep_loss of the first move after the last book move, player's deviations vs opponents' deviations (disjoint sets of games); difference = player minus opponents
findings.caveat: Independent bootstrap over disjoint game sets. In cp_loss: 39 [33, 46] vs 62 [52, 73].

findings.claim: In bullet, the player's result relative to expectation is the same whether the player or the opponent left the named lines first.
findings.metric: mean score minus Elo expected score in games where the player deviated first (player) vs where the opponent deviated first (opponents column holds this control); difference = player-deviated minus opponent-deviated
findings.caveat: The 'opponents' column is the control condition (opponent deviated first), not an opponents' quality number.

findings.claim: In blitz, the player's result relative to expectation is the same whether the player or the opponent left the named lines first.
findings.metric: mean score minus Elo expected score in games where the player deviated first (player) vs where the opponent deviated first (opponents column holds this control); difference = player-deviated minus opponent-deviated
findings.caveat: The 'opponents' column is the control condition (opponent deviated first), not an opponents' quality number.

findings.claim: In rapid, the player's result relative to expectation is the same whether the player or the opponent left the named lines first.
findings.metric: mean score minus Elo expected score in games where the player deviated first (player) vs where the opponent deviated first (opponents column holds this control); difference = player-deviated minus opponent-deviated
findings.caveat: The 'opponents' column is the control condition (opponent deviated first), not an opponents' quality number.
